subject.title: [Feature] Re-enable dev channel distribution tag for npm releases

question: Should the user-facing `dev` channel remain a git checkout of moving `main`, or should OpenClaw add a separately versioned npm snapshot stream under the `dev` dist-tag?
rationale: The current controlled npm `alpha` lane and git-based `dev` path are deliberate, security-sensitive release contracts; code inspection cannot safely choose whether a second bleeding-edge npm stream is worth its supply-chain and user-sem([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.github/workflows/openclaw-npm-release.yml))turn11view3

options.title: Keep dev git-only
options.body: Treat `openclaw update --channel dev` as the canonical moving-main path and remove or tighten documentation that implies an available npm `dev` selector.

options.title: Add versioned npm dev snapshots
options.body: Create a distinct prerelease version scheme, trusted trigger policy, OIDC publish path, registry verification, rollback procedure, and tests before exposing `openclaw@dev`.

options.title: Alias controlled alpha builds
options.body: Point `dev` at approved alpha releases only if maintainers intentionally want both selectors to share identical versions and document that semantic.

recommendation.title: Keep dev git-only
recommendation.body: Treat `openclaw update --channel dev` as the canonical moving-main path and remove or tighten documentation that implies an available npm `dev` selector.
